The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.19794 of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"...to Issue a writ or order/s more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the third respondent in referring the dispute under award dated 24.6.2015 bearing No.B/728/2009-2 under section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act XXX of 2013) in respect of land of the petitioner admeasuring 1 acre 24.75 guntas in survey No.35 of Fathepur Village, Shankarpally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District as being illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional and
be pleased to pass

... " 
2. Heard Sri Vivek Jain, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition.
Perused the record.
3. The petitioners herein claim to be the owners of the land admeasuring 1 acre 24.75 guntas in Sy.No.35 of Fathepur village, Shankarpally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District.

The case of the petitioners is that the said land has been acquired for the purpose of widening and strengthening of Kandi to Shadnagar road, under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 thereafter an award enquiry was initiated and award was also passed on 15.06.2015 vide proceedings No.B/728/2009-2.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Respondent No.3 also determined the compensation of Rs.42,16,972/- for land admeasuring 1 acre 24.75 guntas.

However, when the petitioners went to respondent No.3 for collecting the compensation amount, it was informed that since a title dispute is raised by respondent No.4 (who is the sister of the petitioners) claiming 1/5th share in the land, the compensation amount is deposited in the Civil Court; thus refused to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

The case of the petitioners is that respondent No.4 did not file any claim in respect of the compensation amount of Rs.42,16,972/-, but respondent No.3 appears to have referred the matter under Section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 on the ground that W.P.No.12483 of 2015 is filed by respondent No.4 for referring the matter to the Civil Court pursuant to the award.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is the further case of the petitioners that when objection is not filed by respondent No.4, respondent No.3 does not have any authority to refer the matter to the Civil Court.
Respondent No.3 also failed to see that the interim order, dated 27.04.2015 passed in W.P.No.12483 of 2015 was only to retain 1/5th of the compensation amount not the entire compensation amount.

5. This writ petition is pending before this Court since 9 years.
Till date, no counter-affidavit has been filed by the respondents.

6. Since, it is the case of the petitioners that in the Suit for partition no amount has been granted towards compensation for the lands in Sy.No.35, as such allowing the petitioners to work-out their rights in the partition Suit, compensation amount/equivalent value in the final decree proceedings,
this Writ Petition is dismissed.
There shall be no orders as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The case of the petitioners is that respondent No.4 did not file any claim in respect of the compensation amount of Rs.42,16,972/-, but respondent No.3 appears to have referred the matter under Section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 on the ground that W.P.No.12483 of 2015 is filed by respondent No.4 for referring the matter to the Civil Court pursuant to the award.
It is the further case of the petitioners that when objection is not filed by respondent No.4, respondent No.3 does not have any authority to refer the matter to the Civil Court.
Respondent No.3 also failed to see that the interim order, dated 27.04.2015 passed in W.P.No.12483 of 2015 was only to retain 1/5th of the compensation amount not the entire compensation amount.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that respondent No.4 did not file any claim in respect of the compensation amount of Rs.42,16,972/-, which was determined to be paid to the petitioners.
When objection is not filed by respondent No.4, withholding the compensation amount by respondent No.3 is illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional.
